sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has type-1 mandibles and the largest head capsule among the species of this type. It differs from O. wheeleri, whose soldier has an ocellar spot and shorter mandibles (from the marginal tooth-like process to the apex), from O. aduncus, which is smaller, and from O. tubesauassu, whose lateral projections are smaller and slightly constricted at the base.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head slightly convergent anteriorly in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle prominent in lateral view, situated behind the lateral projection. Mandibles type 1, with a tooth-like process on the proximal half. Head capsule sparsely covered with short hairs and setae, the short hairs denser ventrally, minute hairs scattered over the surface and denser apically. Postmentum with short hairs. Surface of the pronotum with short hairs and the anterior and posterior margins with setae; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs and setae; abdominal tergites with fairly dense short hairs and a few setae on the margins, the sternites with short hairs on the surface and setae on the posterior margin.
